title: Vulkan Compute Pipelines
description: Builds compute pipelines with Vulkan for vendor-neutral GPU acceleration. Explicit control over memory, synchronization, and queues trades verbosity for portability and predictability. One code path runs on all major vendors.

demo.title: Demo — Vulkan Compute Pipelines

title: OpenCL Portability
description: Writes kernels in OpenCL C for the widest device coverage, including CPUs and FPGAs. The platform model abstracts devices; kernels compile at runtime per device. It is the lingua franca of heterogeneous compute.

demo.title: Demo — OpenCL Portability

title: HIP for CUDA Portability
description: Ports CUDA code to HIP for AMD (and NVIDIA) with near-mechanical translation. hipify converts CUDA API calls; the same source builds for both vendors. It rescues CUDA codebases from single-vendor lock-in.

demo.title: Demo — HIP for CUDA Portability

title: SYCL Single-Source
description: Writes single-source C++ with SYCL that offloads to any supported accelerator. Host and device code live in one file; the runtime handles data movement via buffers or USM. It is the modern standard C++ path to GPUs.

demo.title: Demo — SYCL Single-Source

title: Shader Compiler Toolchains
description: Compiles shaders through portable toolchains: GLSL/HLSL to SPIR-V to native. glslang and DXC front-ends plus vendor back-ends make one shader source run everywhere. Offline compilation catches errors early.

demo.title: Demo — Shader Compiler Toolchains

title: Command Buffer Recording
description: Records command buffers once and replays them to amortize CPU overhead. Static workloads record at startup; dynamic ones use per-frame buffers. It is how Vulkan achieves low driver overhead.
key_mechanisms: Use per-frame buffers for dynamic work

demo.title: Demo — Command Buffer Recording

title: GPU Memory Heaps
description: Allocates from the right GPU memory heap: device-local for speed, host-visible for uploads. The memory model exposes heaps and types; the allocator picks per usage. Wrong-heap allocation silently kills performance.

demo.title: Demo — GPU Memory Heaps

title: Multi-GPU Scaling
description: Scales across multiple GPUs with explicit multi-device or NVLink/Infinity Fabric. Work splits by data or model parallel; fast interconnects keep scaling near-linear. It is how large training runs work.

demo.title: Demo — Multi-GPU Scaling

title: Descriptor Set Management
description: Manages Vulkan descriptor sets binding resources to shaders. Layouts declare bindings; pools allocate sets; updates bind buffers and images. Efficient set management avoids a common CPU bottleneck.

demo.title: Demo — Descriptor Set Management

title: GPU Synchronization
description: Synchronizes GPU work with fences, semaphores, and barriers. Fences signal host; semaphores order queues; barriers order within passes. Correct synchronization is the hardest part of explicit APIs.

demo.title: Demo — GPU Synchronization

title: Vendor Extension Handling
description: Uses vendor extensions where they win, with core fallbacks everywhere else. Extensions expose ray tracing or mesh shaders early; the code paths check availability at runtime. It balances bleeding edge with portability.

demo.title: Demo — Vendor Extension Handling

title: GPU Virtualization
description: Shares physical GPUs across VMs with SR-IOV or mediated devices. Each VM gets a virtual GPU with isolated memory; the hypervisor schedules the hardware. Cloud gaming and VDI depend on it.

demo.title: Demo — GPU Virtualization

title: GPU Profiling
description: Profiles GPU workloads with vendor tools to find the real bottleneck. Nsight and RGP show kernel timelines, occupancy, and memory stalls. Optimization without profiling is guessing.

demo.title: Demo — GPU Profiling

title: Compute Fallback Paths
description: Falls back to CPU compute when no suitable GPU exists. The same algorithm runs scalar or SIMD on the CPU; feature detection picks the path at startup. It guarantees the software runs everywhere.

demo.title: Demo — Compute Fallback Paths

title: Cooperative Groups
description: Uses cooperative groups for flexible thread synchronization beyond blocks. Grids can synchronize as a whole for algorithms that need global coordination. It enables patterns blocks cannot express.

demo.title: Demo — Cooperative Groups
